sources.rank_basis: tier A: nodejs.org/api/ (saved page is the Node.js v26.13.1 documentation)

sources.ref: (uncited) Worked example benchmark; Edge cases re-tests on Node 24.22
sources.rank_basis: local experiments described in the doc; no artifact, probe or harness result is in the input

claim_checks.claim: `private` and `protected` are enforced only during type checking. Runtime lookups, and bracket notation even during type checking, still reach the member: it is "soft private".
claim_checks.page_says: private and protected are only enforced during type checking. … private also allows access using bracket notation during type checking. This makes private-declared fields … soft private
claim_checks.note: Runtime lookups reaching private or protected members is entailed. The bracket-notation escape and the "soft private" label are stated for `private` only; the claim's subject extends them to `protected` too. Wider scope.

claim_checks.claim: `#` fields stay private after compilation and have no bracket-notation escape hatch: they are "hard private".
claim_checks.page_says: JavaScript’s private fields (#) remain private after compilation and do not provide the previously mentioned escape hatches like bracket notation access, making them hard private.

claim_checks.claim: When compiling to ES2021 or lower, TypeScript replaces `#` with `WeakMap`s. The handbook notes that these runtime privacy checks will degrade performance.
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #. … Note that these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance.
claim_checks.note: The WeakMap downlevel is entailed. The handbook says the checks "could affect" performance; the claim attributes to the handbook that they "will degrade" it. A could raised to will (MUST level) and put in the source's mouth.

claim_checks.claim: Private elements are not properties. They cannot be enumerated, deleted, proxied, or reached through `Object` methods, and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields.
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method. … For this reason, structuredClone() does not clone private elements
claim_checks.note: The first two sentences are entailed. The structuredClone part inverts the page: MDN says structuredClone() does not clone private elements.

claim_checks.claim: V8 9.4 moved class-field initialization, including private fields, onto its inline-cache fast path. Before that it went through slower runtime calls.
claim_checks.page_says: The first issue has been fixed in V8 v9.7 … Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call for class field initializations.
claim_checks.note: Wrong version: the blog says v9.7, not 9.4 (the doc's own front matter also says V8 ≥ 9.7). The claim also drops the blog's condition that the new IC is used only "when V8 considers the pattern of the initialization to be predictable enough", with a runtime fallback otherwise.

claim_checks.claim: Reading a `#` field from an object whose class did not declare it throws a `TypeError`. `#x in obj` checks for it without throwing.
claim_checks.page_says: If you access a private element from an object that doesn't have the element, a TypeError is thrown … You can use the in operator to check whether an externally defined object possesses a private element.
claim_checks.note: The page's own example error reads "Cannot read private member #x from an object whose class did not declare it", and the in check returns true or false.

claim_checks.claim: An injected collaborator (port, clock, logger) | `private readonly x` constructor parameter | A `#` name cannot be a parameter property
claim_checks.page_says: That this is not possible is a bit surprising
claim_checks.note: The issue comment says `constructor(readonly #text: string) {}` is not possible. Grounded, but [^5] is Rank 6 and this row sits in How it works (role 3, ranks 1–4 allowed): KB-15 breach, recorded in violations. [^1] (Rank 1) lists the only parameter-property modifiers as public, private, protected or readonly and can carry this row instead.

claim_checks.claim: Object wrapped in a `Proxy` (some mocking and reactivity libraries) | `#` access does not go through the proxy | Private elements cannot be proxied
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method.

claim_checks.claim: Target ES2021 or lower | `#` becomes `WeakMap` lookups | TypeScript downlevels it
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #.

claim_checks.claim: Working around it with `--experimental-transform-types` | Runs on Node 24.22 with an `ExperimentalWarning` (re-tested 2026-11-03); the flag is removed in Node 26.0.0 | So code meant to run unbuilt keeps injected collaborators as `readonly #field`s assigned in the constructor
claim_checks.note: Removal in v26.0.0 is entailed. Searched "ExperimentalWarning", "24.22", "transform-types", "parameter properties": the saved v26.13.1 page says nothing about the flag handling parameter properties or about Node 24.22 output. The 24.22 re-test has no probe or artifact in the input, and the "keep collaborators as readonly #fields" advice is the doc's inference.

claim_checks.claim: Type stripping itself | Stable (stability 2) since Node 24.12.0 and 25.2.0; no warning since 24.3.0; Node ignores `tsconfig.json` and needs `.ts` extensions in relative imports | Node only deletes types
claim_checks.page_says: v24.3.0, v22.18.0 | Type stripping no longer emits an experimental warning. … Node.js ignores tsconfig.json files
claim_checks.note: Stability 2 since v25.2.0/v24.12.0, ignored tsconfig.json, mandatory file extensions (`import './file.ts'`) and "only removing inline types" are all entailed. "No warning" drops the page's qualifier "experimental".

conflicts.topic: Cost of creating `#` fields versus public fields
conflicts.winner: [^3] rank 4: the IC fast path exists only from V8 v9.7, and only when the initialization pattern is predictable; before v9.7 initialization used costly runtime calls
conflicts.loser: local benchmark (rank local, Node 24.22 / V8 13.6), generalised in the Summary to any "native ES2022+ target" and in Takeaways to "an ES2022+ target"
conflicts.note: Not an open conflict: the front matter bounds the doc to V8 ≥ 9.7 (Node ≥ 18) and How it works 6 states the earlier slow path. But How it works 6 gives the wrong version (C5), and the Summary and Takeaway sentences drop the V8 bound, so read alone they cover engines the blog says were slower.

violations.evidence: C3: item 3 says the handbook notes the runtime privacy checks "will degrade performance"; [^1] says they "could affect performance".
C4: item 4 says `structuredClone()` copies private elements like public fields; [^2] says "structuredClone() does not clone private elements".
C5: item 6 says V8 9.4; [^3] says the fix shipped in V8 v9.7 ("Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call"). It also drops the "predictable enough" condition.
The "Where each form fits" table cites [^5] (github.com issue, Rank 6) for "A `#` name cannot be a parameter property"; role 3 allows ranks 1–4.
C1: item 1 applies bracket-notation access and the "soft private" label to both `private` and `protected`; [^1] states them for `private` only.
[^6] (TC39 class fields proposal) is listed as backing How it works 2 but is never cited in the body; item 2 cites only [^1].
C10: the Node 24.22 ExperimentalWarning re-test and the workaround advice are not in [^4]; only the v26.0.0 removal is. No probe or artifact for the re-test is in the input.
C11: "no warning since 24.3.0"; [^4] says type stripping "no longer emits an experimental warning" (v24.3.0, v22.18.0).

"On a native ES2022+ target, reading and creating # fields costs the same as public fields" (and the matching Takeaway) carries no V8 bound; [^3] says initialization was much slower before v9.7 and uses the fast path only for predictable patterns. The front matter's V8 ≥ 9.7 is the only bound.
The "Where each form fits" decision table (which form to choose per field kind) is choice guidance, not mechanism; it belongs with the Trade-offs table (role 6).

The run reports timings and outputs but shows neither the benchmark code nor a link to an artifact or probe, so the measurement cannot be reproduced from the doc. The same holds for "Reproduced on Node 24.22" in Edge cases.
Says "Verified: 10 claims (✅)"; the body carries 11 ✅ marks (How it works 1–6, the parameter-property row, and four Edge cases rows).

patch_instructions.action: Item 1: limit the bracket escape and the label to `private`: "`private` and `protected` are enforced only during type checking, so runtime lookups still reach them. `private` also allows bracket-notation access during type checking, which makes it 'soft private'. ✅[^1]"

Item 3: replace "will degrade performance" with "could affect performance", as [^1] words it ("these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance"), and note that the handbook says this of runtime privacy mechanisms in general (closures, WeakMaps, private fields).
Item 4: replace "and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields" with "`structuredClone()` does not clone them, and `Object.freeze()` and `Object.seal()` have no effect on them ✅[^2]".

Item 6: change "V8 9.4" to "V8 v9.7" and add the condition from [^3]: the new IC is used when V8 sees a predictable initialization pattern; otherwise it falls back to a runtime call. Optionally add that the work shipped in Node.js 18.0.0 ([^3]).

"Where each form fits", injected-collaborator row: replace ✅[^5] with ✅[^1] and word it from the handbook's Parameter Properties section: "parameter properties are created only with `public`, `private`, `protected` or `readonly`, so a `#` name cannot be one". Keep [^5] only in a role 6 section (for example as the open feature request) or drop it. Consider moving the whole table under ## Trade-offs.
Either cite [^6] in How it works 2 alongside [^1] (the proposal says it is "impossible to access the private field from outside of the class"), or remove the [^6] entry.

`--experimental-transform-types` row: keep ✅[^4] only on "the flag is removed in Node 26.0.0". Mark the Node 24.22 ExperimentalWarning result ⚠️ or back it with a probe or artifact that is cited, and present "keep injected collaborators as readonly #fields" as the doc's recommendation without a ✅.
Type stripping row: change "no warning since 24.3.0" to "no experimental warning since 24.3.0 (and 22.18.0)" per [^4].

Bound the performance sentence: "On a native ES2022+ target in V8 ≥ 9.7 (Node ≥ 18), reading and creating # fields measured the same as public fields (Node 24.22)", and make the matching Takeaway say the same; [^3] gives the v9.7 boundary.
Add the benchmark code (or a cited artifact or probe) so the inputs of each measured case are visible.
Recount the ✅ marks after the fixes above; the current body has 11, not 10.
